title: A singular noun never goes out alone
rule: A singular countable noun needs a, an, the, or a word like my or this in front of it.
mnemonic: One thing, one helper: if you can count it and there is one, give it an article.
examples: I bought car → I bought a car | He is engineer → He is an engineer

title: Find the subject, then match the verb
rule: He, she, it and singular nouns take a verb ending in -s in the present tense.
examples: She go to work → She goes to work
